App recommendations. I really enjoy the ease of use of this app it’s intuitive and makes note-taking simple and efficient. One improvement I’d strongly recommend is reconsidering the placement of the delete button in the notes feature. Having it available while actively writing has led to several unfortunate moments where I’ve accidentally lost hard-earned notes by lightly grazing the delete option.
It would be much safer to move the delete function to the main notes list, placing it to the right of each note instead. Additionally, adding an undo feature would be incredibly helpful, along with bullet-point formatting options for better note organization.
If removing the delete button from the writing screen isn’t an option, I suggest adding a confirmation step such as a “Are you sure?” prompt before a note is permanently deleted. These changes would greatly improve the user experience and prevent accidental data loss.

It isn't perfect.. Greek and Hebrew are very economical languages. You can say more meaning in Greek and Hebrew with fewer words than you can in English or American style English. When the translators of the Bible tried to bring the ancient languages into English they took the admonishment not to add to or detract from what the Word of God was saying as to mean that they needed to give a one word for one word translation. But to do this you have to leave out some of the meaning of the ancient words. What the translators of the Amplified Bible tried to do was to include all the embedded meaning of the ancient words. This can result in a single ancient word being translated into two, three, or even four modern words to convey the entire meaning. This is, for the most part, a restating of what is in the forward of the Amplified Bible.

If it does have a flaw, at least in my opinion, it is when it includes what the translators believed were implied meanings. It is my view that the translators were not necessarily wrong as much as they were limiting. There are times when I am reading it that I believe that it is bigger than the meaning they have given it. Bigger, more all encompassing, more universal, greater…

There are reasons, scriptural reasons, that I have for this particular belief. The words and promises of the Lord are pure words, like silver tried an earth in furnace, purified seven times, for example. That is from Isaiah. And there are more but I won't go into that. For me, personally, it is my study Bible, and has been for over 40 years. KLT
